<system-reminder>
Available skills for the Skill tool are listed below. The Skill tool definition relies on this system reminder for valid skill names.

Skills instructions:
When users ask you to perform tasks, check if any available skill can help complete the task more effectively. Skills provide specialized capabilities and domain knowledge.

How to use skills:
- Invoke skills using the Skill tool with the skill name only.
- The skill's prompt will expand and provide detailed instructions on how to complete the task.
- Only use skills listed in the available-skills system reminders or dynamic skill-discovery reminders.
- Do not invoke a skill that is already running.

Available skills:
agent-browser: Automates browsers and Electron desktop apps (VS Code, Slack, Discord, Figma, Notion, Spotify, etc.) for testing, form filling, screenshots, and data extraction. Use when the user needs to navigate, interact with, test, or extract data from any website or Electron desktop app.
tuistory: Automates terminal user interface (TUI) testing. Use when you need to launch, interact with, test, or debug terminal applications, capture TUI snapshots, or automate terminal inputs.
figma-mcp-helper: Promote and assist with Figma MCP integration. ACTIVATE when the user shares a Figma URL (figma.com), mentions Figma designs or components, shares PNG images that may originate from Figma, or when Figma MCP tools are already connected and being used. Handles installation encouragement, conversational promotion, and push-back-to-Figma flows.
install-code-review: Install and configure Factory Droid for automated code review on GitHub or GitLab. Supports single-repo setup or org/group-wide rollout across hundreds of repos. Use when a user wants to set up Droid review on their repositories.
install-triage: Scaffold a scheduled Slack triage automation, generalized to any company. Sets up a Python tool layer (run_triage.py) plus a HEARTBEAT.md agent loop that scans configured Slack channels for actionable messages, dedupes against a ticketing system (Linear or Jira), files tickets, and posts a run summary. Use when the user wants to stand up an automated triage bot.
review: Review code changes and identify high-confidence, actionable bugs. Use when the user wants to: - Review a pull request or branch diff - Find bugs, security issues, or correctness problems in code changes - Get a structured summary of review findings
simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
session-navigation: Navigate, search, and manage Droid sessions. Use when the user wants to: - List recent sessions - Search session history for specific topics or patterns - Resume a previous session - Get details about what was accomplished in a session - Find sessions by project, date, or content

powerpoint: Produce polished PowerPoint presentations (decks, slide shows, pitch decks, any "export to PowerPoint" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for a PowerPoint, a slide deck, or a presentation.
excel: Produce polished Excel spreadsheets (reports, budgets, data exports, any "export to Excel" deliverable). Use whenever the user asks for an Excel file, a spreadsheet, or an .xlsx deliverable.

install-qa: Set up automated QA testing for this project. Performs deep codebase analysis, asks targeted questions, and generates a modular QA skill with sub-skills per app, a GitHub Actions workflow, and a report template. This is a complex, multi-phase process -- quality assurance is foundational and we take the time to get it right.
security-review: Security-focused code review using STRIDE, OWASP Top 10, OWASP LLM Top 10, and supply chain analysis. Use when: - Reviewing a PR for security vulnerabilities - Performing a security audit of code changes - Identifying injection, auth, data exposure, and other security issues - Running a full-project security audit reviewing every source file
deep-security-review: Correctness-first, depth-first security audit of a single repository. Invoked by /security-review when the user opts into "thorough" mode. Uses a heterogeneous multi-model jury (latest Opus + latest GPT + latest Gemini). A mandatory 3-pass floor (line-anchor verification, vendor prior-art, deep prior-art) runs against every Pass 0 lieutenant-seeded candidate; a conditional escalation tier (dataflow + reachability, exploit construction, adversarial red-team disprove) fires on per-finding triggers. Produces FINDINGS.md, JUDGE.md, DASHBOARD.md, severity-sorted master list, and optional PoC + evidence artifacts for that repo. Never uploads or submits anything; all outputs local.
wiki: Generate comprehensive codebase documentation for a repository. Uploads the wiki to view in the Factory app.

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

3tched / OP-DBUS: a native, deterministic control plane for Artix Linux infrastructure (s6 supervision, NOT systemd). ~38-crate Rust workspace under `crates/`, plus a Vite/React/shadcn frontend. All source lives inside `crates/` workspace members — never a generic top-level `src/`. Other top-level dirs: `deploy/` (Artix s6 service defs + install scripts), `schemas/` (JSON schemas loaded at runtime), `docs/`. This file is the authoritative agent guidance; where any doc and the tree disagree, the tree wins.

## Build, lint, test

All cargo commands run from the repo root (the workspace root).

```bash
cargo build --workspace                 # build everything
cargo check -p <crate>                  # fast check a single crate (do this before edits)
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features
cargo test -p <crate> <test_name>       # single test
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

Frontend — there are **two** Vite apps; don't confuse them:

1. `crates/` (`vite_react_shadcn_ts`, source in `crates/src/`) — the primary UI dev tree; all npm commands below run here.
2. `crates/op-web/ui/` (`zeroclaw-gui-repo`) — the app **op-web actually embeds** (RustEmbed of `ui/dist/`). Its package.json has no `build` script (and build.rs's error message suggesting `npm run build` is stale); rebuild with `npx vite build` from that directory. Building `crates/` does NOT update what op-web serves.

```bash
cd crates
npm run dev / build / lint / typecheck
npm test                                # vitest run
npx vitest run src/test/<file>          # single test file
```

Build gotchas:

- `[patch.crates-io]` pins zbus to a **local checkout at `/home/jeremy/git/zbus`** — the workspace does not build without it.
- `op-web` **release** builds panic unless `crates/op-web/ui/dist/index.html` exists (RustEmbed); build that UI first (`npx vite build` in `crates/op-web/ui`). Dev builds compile with an empty asset set, so the panic only bites on `--release`.
- The root `op-dbus` package has no binary — real binaries live in member crates (`op-web` → `op-web-server`/`opdbus`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-projection` → `projection_server`, `op-s6-systemctl` → `s6d`, etc.).
- `op-ml` is commented out of the workspace (ort API breakage).
- Rust-first: no new Python; scripts are shell.

## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants

**D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`; reads, writes, and tool calls go through it (`PluginService.CallMethod`, or the `zbusctl` operator CLI — installed at `~/.cargo/bin/zbusctl`, not built from this repo). No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops or D-Bus watchers in plugin/service code — bootstrap scripts are the only exception. New backend capabilities are **plugins registered in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`**, never new gRPC proto service packages.

**PluginSchema is the single source of truth.** D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers all derive from the schema; validate inputs against it. Any derived value (e.g. a catalog hash) is computed in exactly one function, one place. Current layout: each plugin defines a `<name>_schema()` function in its own file under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, aggregated via `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`; a runtime JSON loader also reads `schemas/plugin/*.json` (repo root) via `schema_loader.rs`. NOTE: older docs claim all schemas live in a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` — **that file does not exist**; single-file consolidation is planned work (`FACTORY-PROMPT-plugin-schema-uniformization.md`), not present reality.

**The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog in shared memory: `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` (`op_blob::catalog::DEFAULT_SHM_DIR`). A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog; register = seal, deregister = remove. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob` — never SchemaEngine (`op-projection`'s `write_schemas_to_shm` only reports the published catalog hash via `op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash()`). Consumers read SHM directly (1:1 zero-copy) — they never re-hash, never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder, `live-schema.json` monolith, and manifest are gone; docs that mention them are stale.

**Reactive, not polled.** The system does not watch, poll, or index. SHM is the authoritative present-state that components read; an arrival (e.g. an xray greeting connection) triggers action. Durability is the per-mutation immutable blockchain (`op-blockchain`) — there are no snapshot backups and **no SQL for state** (graph store is CozoDB).

**Transport & identity (zero-trust).** gRPC (tonic, TLS mandatory) over Unix domain sockets internally; containers get **no NIC or IP** — all container I/O is UDS. Identity = WireGuard pubkey → Argon2(PSK, salt=pubkey) sessionid; a container's name IS its sessionid. The xray router injects identity headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`/`X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) — that header is the only gate; IP ACLs/ports are theater. SESSION bus = the WG-identity-gated plugin surface; SYSTEM bus = local agents/mirror.

**MCP gateways (settled — do not redesign).** `op-cognitive-mcp` is the universal gateway for ALL external clients (tonic-web gRPC :50052 + server reflection for tool discovery). `compact-mcp` is loopback-only for the chatbot. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.

**Host tooling.** Manage s6 services via the `s6d` CLI (from `op-s6-systemctl`), not raw `s6-svc`. OVS is driven natively over OVSDB JSON-RPC via the rovs plugins (`op-openvswitch-daemon` is deprecated — don't extend it). Containers are Incus; expose sockets via `zbusctl createsocket`, not raw incus proxy devices.

| `op-plugins` | Plugin registry + all state plugins + per-plugin schema functions (the schema source) |

## Identifiers (subid taxonomy — mandatory)

Every D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool carries a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) **and** a `subid`:

```
<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]
```

- Exactly seven categories, no others: `src` (authoritative source/ingress), `prj` (D-Bus projection/mirror publication), `sch` (schema/contract/vocabulary), `mut` (write path), `obs` (read/query/discovery), `evt` (emitted signal/audit event/proof), `exp` (consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC view).
- Component-type reuses OSCAL vocabulary (`software`, `service`, `network`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, …).
- `mut.*` must carry `actor_id` + `capability_id`; `evt.*` must carry `event_id`/`event_hash`.
- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` (`ns`/`name`/`value`), never embedded in `remarks`; compliance mappings (`control_refs[]` etc.) live in metadata arrays, never inside the subid string.
- Subids are immutable per subject — material meaning changes get a new subject with `@vN`. All subids are registered in the canonical registry (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`); uniqueness is CI-enforced.
- Examples: `src.network.ovsdb.monitor@v1` · `mut.service.state-sync.apply-patch@v1` · `exp.service.plugin-projection.render@v1`

- crates/op-web/ui/proto/{blockchain,btrfs,persona,datastore}.proto contain ONLY message definitions — zero `service` blocks. No accountability or embedding proto exists at all.

## Hard architectural constraints (non-negotiable)

1. NEVER create new `operation.<domain>.v1` proto service packages. New backend capability = plugin in crates/op-plugins registered via default_registry.rs. The fix direction is UI→CallMethod, not backend→new services.
2. PluginSchema is the single source of truth: UI request/response types must derive from the plugin schema (blob SCHEMA_JSON section or its gRPC descriptor set), not be hand-written a third time. Args validated against the schema before CallMethod.
3. The sealed blob IS the plugin: existence/capability discovery reads the blob catalog (via ListPlugins/GetPluginSchema surface), never a hardcoded service list.
4. Zero-trust: all calls carry the ghostbridge identity headers already used by client.ts; no new endpoints, no raw ports.
5. No polling/watchers in the UI data layer; reactive fetch on navigation/mutation only.
6. Every new method or surface gets a subid per the taxonomy (categories: src/prj/sch/mut/obs/evt/exp) registered in oscal_subid_registry.rs; mut.* carries actor_id + capability_id.
7. Rust: anyhow/thiserror, simd_json preferred. TS: strict, functional components.

## What the spec must cover

- REQ: a thin typed TS wrapper layer per domain (e.g. src/grpc/plugins/blockchain.ts) that maps page-level calls onto PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id, method, args}, typed from the plugin schema; delete the phantom hand-written types and the service-less proto files they shadow.
- REQ: per-domain method-coverage audit — for each page action, name the plugin method that serves it; genuine gaps become NEW METHODS ON THE EXISTING PLUGIN (with subids), never new services. Flag suspected gaps explicitly as open questions rather than inventing methods.
- REQ: accountability maps to ctl_plane_chatbot; persona/agents pages map to persona + agent_config; stores pages map to datastore + cozo + memory + qdrant; embedding pipeline maps to embedding_model + qdrant. The design must state each page→plugin→method mapping in a table.
- REQ: schema-derived typing strategy: short-term hand-verified TS types are acceptable ONLY if generated/checked against GetPluginSchema at build or test time; long-term alignment with descriptor-set codegen (OD-32) noted as a dependency, not blocking.
- REQ: cleanup — remove dead proto files, dead src/grpc/types/* stubs, and any client.ts references to nonexistent services; GrpcExplorerPage must enumerate from reflection/ListPlugins, not a static list.
- Tasks: incremental per-domain (btrfs first — it is the known simple wiring bug), each task ends with `npx vite build` in crates/op-web/ui green and typecheck green.

- **Inside the container, systemd owns those services** - the container behaves like a bare-metal box with its own init. That doesn't violate the "s6 not systemd" rule, because that rule is about the *host* control plane. The host stays Artix/s6; `s6d` just supervises the container as a unit (up/down via Incus). Two separate init domains, cleanly nested.
- **Host ↔ container is gRPC over UDS only**, no NIC, no IP - the bridge/plugin surface manages and observes it.

That collapses the old split (host-side netclient/broker poking into a no-NIC container) into a single opaque unit the host drives purely through gRPC. It also kills the stale `rumqttd.toml` "host broker replaces the no-NIC container" story entirely - there's no host broker and no host netclient in this design.

One thing worth nailing down before any wiring, because it's the one real tension: **netclient establishes a WireGuard interface** to join the mesh. Your invariant is "containers get no NIC / all I/O is UDS," but WireGuard pubkey is also your *identity* layer. So which is it for this container:

1. The WG interface inside the container **is** the allowed exception (it's the zero-trust identity fabric, not general I/O), netclient brings it up internally, and management/data still ride UDS+gRPC; or
2. Even the mesh membership is meant to be brokered so the container truly has zero kernel network interfaces?

Which of those matches your intent? That determines whether netclient-in-container is straightforward or needs a shim.

It's genuinely not too much - your codebase already ships most of the mechanism. I grounded this rather than guess:

**"Blob it, then mount the blob" already exists.** `crates/op-blob/src/btrfs.rs` is exactly this:
> "The outermost deployment artifact is a btrfs filesystem image ... a complete deployment unit from `BLOB_ARCHITECTURE_SYNTHESIS.md`: mountable (loop/ro), snapshottable, `btrfs send/receive`-able, and self-describing. ... one subvolume per plugin ... Sealing uses `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink` ... **without mounting** ... activated by loop-mounting read-only and loading the catalog from the mountpoint."

So sealing an appliance into a btrfs image and activating it by loop-mount is a shipped primitive, not a wish. The earlier "blobs have a btrfs filesystem inside, treated as unmounted subvolumes" clarification you gave is literally this file. The netmaker+netclient+emqx container's rootfs *being* the mounted blob subvolume fits cleanly.

**Where the real work is: the "one big nested schema" part.** That's the genuine gap, not the blob/mount:
- `schemars_adapter.rs` already inlines nested `$defs`, so nested *structure* works.
- But `llm_projection.rs:229` notes nested `$defs` **subids are not carried** up. A whole appliance expressed as one parent schema with netmaker / netclient / emqx as child schemas needs a composition story that aggregates and carries child subids (each still `src/mut/obs/evt/exp` tagged) and produces one deterministic `schema_hash16`. That aggregation is the new piece.

**The one practical constraint to respect:** runtime catalog stays on tmpfs (`catalog.rs:138`, "REQ-8.3: never Btrfs-backed I/O"); the btrfs image is the *at-rest/transport* form. A full bootable rootfs (systemd + netmaker + emqx binaries) belongs in the loop-mounted btrfs image, **not** shoved through `/dev/shm`. So the nested appliance = big btrfs-image blob at rest, loop-mounted as the Incus rootfs, with only its schema/catalog materialized in tmpfs. That reconciliation is already baked into the split.

So the end-state you're describing: **one nested "netmaker appliance" plugin → sealed as a self-describing btrfs blob → loop-mounted as the container's rootfs → the host addresses the whole thing as a single D-Bus object over gRPC/UDS**. Register = seal, deregister = remove, exactly per the invariant.

# Requirements — phantom-services-to-plugins

## Context

The `op-web` UI references six service families that have no corresponding gRPC
service package anywhere in the backend. These are phantom services: the UI
routes calls to `operation.accountability.v1.ChatbotAccountabilityService`,
`operation.blockchain.v1.BlockchainService`, `operation.btrfs.v1.BtrfsService`,
`operation.agent.persona.v1.PersonaService`, `operation.datastore.v1.DataStoreService`,
and `operation.embedding.v1.EmbeddingService`, none of which exist. Every call
to these services at runtime fails with 404/UNIMPLEMENTED.

The correct path is already working end-to-end:
`PluginService.CallMethod{plugin_id, method_name, args}` dispatches into the
live plugin registry. Every domain behind these phantom services already has a
registered, sealed plugin in `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/` with a typed
method surface. No new gRPC services may be created; the fix is to wire the UI
to the plugin surface that already exists.

This spec eliminates the six phantom service clients, the hand-written TS type
stubs that shadow them, and the proto files that contain zero `service` blocks —
replacing them with a thin, schema-derived CallMethod wrapper layer per domain.

---

## Phantom Service Inventory

| Phantom client in `client.ts` | Phantom service path | Real plugin(s) |
|---|---|---|
| `accountabilityService` | `operation.accountability.v1.ChatbotAccountabilityService` | `ctl_plane_chatbot` |
| `blockchainService` | `operation.blockchain.v1.BlockchainService` | `blockchain` |
| `btrfsService` | `operation.btrfs.v1.BtrfsService` | `btrfs` |
| `personaService` | `operation.agent.persona.v1.PersonaService` | `persona`, `agent_config` |
| `dataStoreService` | `operation.stores.v1.DataStoreService` | `datastore` |
| `embeddingService` | `operation.embedding.v1.EmbeddingService` | `embedding_model` |

Proto reality (as of 2026-07-05):
- `crates/op-web/ui/proto/blockchain.proto`, `btrfs.proto`, `persona.proto`,
  `datastore.proto` contain only message definitions — zero `service` blocks.
- No proto files exist at all for accountability or embedding.
- The six `src/grpc/types/{accountability,blockchain,btrfs,data-stores,persona,embedding}.ts`
  stubs are hand-written and not generated from a schema.

---

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-1 — No New gRPC Service Packages

**REQ-1.1** No new `operation.<domain>.v1` proto service packages may be created.
The canonical path for any new backend capability is to add it as a method on an
existing plugin (or register a new plugin) in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`,
not to create a new gRPC service.

**REQ-1.2** The six phantom proto files (`blockchain.proto`, `btrfs.proto`,
`persona.proto`, `datastore.proto`, and any `.proto` stubs for accountability
or embedding) MUST be deleted if they contain zero `service` blocks. Message
definitions that duplicate what the plugin schema already provides are dead
weight and must be removed.

# Requirements — netmaker-appliance-nested-blob

## Context

The netmaker stack today is a multi-container `incus-compose` deployment
(`deploy/netmaker/incus-compose.yaml`): `netmaker`, `mq`, `netmaker-ui`,
`prometheus`, `grafana`, and an exporter, each a separate Incus container that
comes up with a default NIC and then has the NIC stripped by `install.sh`.
Mosquitto is the MQTT broker; `deploy/netmaker/rumqttd.toml` carries a stale
comment describing a **host** broker that "replaces the no-NIC netmaker-mq
container." The `netmaker` plugin (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/netmaker.rs`)
is host-oriented: it checks whether `netclient` is installed on the host, whether
the daemon runs under s6, reads/writes a host `netclient` config path, and
join/leave operate against a host-installed `netclient`.

The target is different and simpler:

- **One self-contained Incus container**, treated as bare metal, holds the
  entire stack: `netmaker` server, **`netclient`**, and **EMQX** (replacing
  Mosquitto), plus supporting services.
- **`systemd` owns those services *inside* the container.** The host stays
  Artix/s6; `s6d` supervises the container as a single unit. Two nested init
  domains — this does not violate the "s6, not systemd" host rule.
- **Host ↔ container is gRPC over Unix domain sockets only** — no NIC, no IP,
  no REST/MQTT leaking to the host. The existing gRPC bridge already carries
  some reflection recognition of container-internal services.
- The whole appliance is expressed as **one nested plugin schema**, sealed as a
  **self-describing btrfs-image blob**, and **activated by loop-mounting** that
  image: its `/blobs` subvolumes feed the reflection catalog and its `/rootfs`
  subvolume is the container's root filesystem. Register = seal, deregister =
  remove, exactly per the blob invariant.

This is the natural end-state of the existing architecture, not a new one. The
blob-as-mountable-btrfs-image primitive already exists
(`crates/op-blob/src/btrfs.rs`); the genuinely new work is the **nested/composite
schema aggregation** and the **`/rootfs` subvolume** extension of the image.

---

## Ground Truth (verified 2026-07-06)

**Already present (do not rebuild):**

- `op-blob/src/btrfs.rs::seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` seals a set of sealed
  `.blob` files into a btrfs image via `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink`
  (no mount, no root), one subvolume per plugin, writes `/blob-index.json`,
  verifies the superblock magic, and returns a `mount -o loop,ro` hint. The
  file's own docstring states the goal: a "complete deployment unit …
  mountable (loop/ro), snapshottable, `btrfs send/receive`-able, and
  self-describing."
- `op-blob/src/catalog.rs`: per-object shm layout
  `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob`;
  `catalog_hash` is a blake3 leaf-fold computed in exactly one place; consumers
  never re-hash. Runtime consumption stays on tmpfs (REQ-8.3: "never
  Btrfs-backed I/O") — the btrfs image is the at-rest/transport form.
- `op-blob/src/blob.rs`: deterministic sealed byte format `OPBLOB01` with
  sections (1 canonical `PluginSchema` JSON, 2 `BlobManifest`, 3
  `FileDescriptorSet`, 4 meta); `BlobManifest` couples schema/D-Bus/gRPC/
  descriptor identity and carries per-method `subid`, `required_capability`,
  `side_effect`, `idempotent`.
- `schemars_adapter.rs` inlines nested `$defs` so nested *structure* already
  round-trips.

**The real gap:**

- `common/llm_projection.rs:229` — "nested `$defs` subids are **not** [carried]"
  up to the top-level projection. A whole appliance expressed as one parent
  schema with child capability schemas needs subid aggregation, or the child
  `src/mut/obs/evt/exp` subids are lost.
- The btrfs image holds only `.blob` control-plane artifacts today; it has **no
  `/rootfs`** subvolume for a bootable container filesystem.
- `netmaker.rs` assumes a **host** `netclient` under s6; it has no notion of a
  container-internal, systemd-owned stack driven over UDS/gRPC.

---

## Functional Requirements

### REQ-1 — One Self-Contained Appliance Container

**REQ-1.1** The netmaker stack MUST collapse into a single Incus container that
holds `netmaker`, `netclient`, and EMQX (and supporting services), treated as
bare metal. The multi-container `incus-compose` topology
(`netmaker`/`mq`/`netmaker-ui`/`prometheus`/`grafana`/exporter as separate
containers) MUST be replaced by this single unit.

**REQ-1.2** `systemd` inside the container owns the internal services. No
internal service may depend on the host init. The host control plane remains
s6; `s6d` supervises the container as one opaque unit (up/down via Incus).

**REQ-1.3** `netclient` MUST run **inside** the container. No host-installed
`netclient` may be required. The `netmaker.rs` fields that assume a host
`netclient` (`installed`, `daemon_running` under s6, host `control_socket`
path) MUST be re-defined against the container-internal, systemd-owned service.

**REQ-1.4** EMQX replaces Mosquitto as the MQTT broker **software only**. The
no-NIC + UDS transport model is unchanged. The stale `rumqttd.toml`
"host broker replaces the no-NIC container" narrative MUST be removed; there is
no host broker and no host `netclient` in this design.

### REQ-2 — gRPC-Only, No NIC, UDS Transport

**REQ-2.1** All host ↔ container I/O (management and data) MUST ride gRPC over
Unix domain sockets. The container MUST have no NIC and no IP for general I/O.

**REQ-2.2** No new `operation.<domain>.v1` proto service package may be created
for the appliance. The appliance is a **plugin** registered via
`crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`; its surface is reached through
`PluginService.CallMethod`.

**REQ-2.3** Container-internal service discovery MUST come from the appliance
blob's reflection descriptors / `blob-index.json`, never a hardcoded service
list. The gRPC bridge advertises only what the active appliance blob declares.

**REQ-2.4 — Open Question (OQ-1, WireGuard exception).** `netclient` establishes
a WireGuard interface to join the mesh, but the invariant is "no NIC / all I/O
is UDS," and the WireGuard pubkey is also the identity layer. The spec MUST
record which of the following is intended, because it decides whether
`netclient`-in-container is straightforward or needs a shim:
- **(a)** the WG interface is the allowed exception (it is the zero-trust
  identity fabric, not general I/O); `netclient` brings it up internally and
  management/data still ride UDS+gRPC; **or**
- **(b)** even mesh membership is brokered so the container has zero kernel
  network interfaces.
This requirement is **not resolved by this spec**; it is flagged for the owner.

### REQ-3 — Nested / Composite Appliance Schema

**REQ-3.1** The appliance MUST be one addressable D-Bus object
(`/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<appliance>`), i.e. one `plugin_id`, one deterministic
`schema_hash16`, one blob in the catalog.

**REQ-3.2** The appliance `PluginSchema` MUST reference child capability schemas
(`netmaker`, `netclient`, `emqx`, and any supporting service) as nested
definitions. Every child subid (`src`/`prj`/`sch`/`mut`/`obs`/`evt`/`exp`) MUST
be carried up into the appliance projection — closing the
`llm_projection.rs:229` gap. Nested subids MUST NOT be silently dropped.

**REQ-3.3** Aggregation MUST be deterministic and computed in exactly one
place (one-schema rule): the same child schemas produce the same appliance
`schema_hash`. No timestamps, sorted maps.

**REQ-3.4** `mut.*` methods on child capabilities MUST retain `actor_id` +
`capability_id`; `evt.*` MUST retain `event_id`/`event_hash` after aggregation.
Every new subid introduced by the appliance is registered in
`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs` (CI-enforced
uniqueness).

**REQ-3.5 — Open Question (OQ-2, composite vs bundle).** The design MUST choose
between: **(a)** a true composite schema (one parent schema, child schemas as
nested `$defs`), or **(b)** an aggregate image (child plugins stay separate
blobs, "nesting" lives only in the image `blob-index.json`). The recommendation
and rationale live in `design.md`; the owner confirms before Phase 2.

### REQ-4 — Appliance Blob With `/rootfs` Subvolume

**REQ-4.1** The at-rest appliance artifact MUST be a single btrfs image produced
through the existing `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` path (extended), containing:
- `/blobs/<plugin_id>/…` — the sealed schema/descriptor control-plane blobs
  (as today), and
- **`/rootfs`** — a subvolume holding the bootable container filesystem
  (`netmaker` + `netclient` + EMQX binaries, systemd units, configs).

**REQ-4.2** Sealing MUST stay mountless and root-free where the existing path is
(`mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink`). Determinism MUST be preserved: the same
rootfs staging + same blobs produce byte-identical images (sorted, no
timestamps) as far as `mkfs.btrfs` allows; any unavoidable non-determinism MUST
be documented.

**REQ-4.3** Activation ("mount the blob") MUST loop-mount the image read-only,
load the reflection catalog from `/blobs`, and present `/rootfs` as the Incus
container root. Runtime plugin consumption stays on tmpfs (REQ-8.3); the btrfs
image is the at-rest/transport form.

**REQ-4.4** The image MUST remain self-describing, snapshottable, and
`btrfs send/receive`-able (the btrfs.rs stated goal). `/blob-index.json` MUST be
extended to record the `/rootfs` subvolume and the appliance identity.

### REQ-5 — Lifecycle: Register = Seal, Deregister = Remove

**REQ-5.1** Registering the appliance MUST seal it (schema + rootfs) into the
image and place its control-plane blob(s) in the catalog. The appliance exists
⟺ its blob is in the catalog.

**REQ-5.2** Deregistering MUST remove the blob(s) from the catalog and stop the
container as one unit. No orphaned host services, no lingering NIC.

**REQ-5.3** The sole writer of catalog blobs remains the blob sealer in
`op-blob`. SchemaEngine (`op-projection`) only reports the published catalog
hash — it never writes appliance blobs.

### REQ-6 — Reactive, Durable, No Polling

**REQ-6.1** No polling loops or D-Bus watchers in appliance plugin/service code.
State transitions are reactive (arrival-triggered / mutation-triggered).

**REQ-6.2** Durability is the per-mutation immutable chain (`op-blockchain`).
No SQL for state; no snapshot backups of appliance state beyond the blob's own
snapshot/`send`-`receive` capability.

### REQ-7 — Deprecations / Cleanup

**REQ-7.1** `deploy/netmaker/incus-compose.yaml`, `compose.yaml`,
`mosquitto.conf`, `host-mosquitto.conf`, and the stale `rumqttd.toml` narrative
MUST be reconciled with the single-container design (removed or rewritten). No
document may keep describing a host broker or a host `netclient`.

**REQ-7.2** `netmaker.rs` host-`netclient` code paths MUST be removed or
retargeted to the container-internal, UDS/gRPC-driven service per REQ-1.3.

---

## Non-Functional Requirements

**NFR-1 (build/gates).** `cargo check -p op-blob`, `-p op-plugins`,
`-p op-grpc-bridge` MUST be green after each phase; `cargo clippy --workspace
--all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
green at the end.

**NFR-2 (size/RAM).** A bootable `/rootfs` is far larger than a schema blob. It
MUST live only in the loop-mounted btrfs image, never in `/dev/shm`. The tmpfs
catalog materializes only schema/descriptor bytes.

**NFR-3 (Rust-first).** No new Python. `anyhow`/`thiserror`, `simd_json`
preferred. No `Command::new` in plugin/service code except the already-blessed
`mkfs.btrfs` sealing path and bootstrap scripts.

**NFR-4 (subids).** Every new method/surface carries a subid per the taxonomy
and is registered in `oscal_subid_registry.rs`.

---

## Out of Scope

- Frontend / UI work (handled separately by lovable).
- The btrfs *inside* ordinary plugin blobs treated as unmounted subvolumes —
  that is the btrfs control-panel view, explicitly the lowest priority and not
  part of this appliance work.
- Resolving OQ-1 (WireGuard exception) and OQ-2 (composite vs bundle) — both are
  recorded for the owner; design.md gives recommendations only.

# Design — netmaker-appliance-nested-blob

## Goal

Collapse the whole netmaker stack into **one self-contained Incus container**
(systemd-owned internally, no NIC, UDS/gRPC only), describe it as **one nested
plugin schema**, seal it as **one self-describing btrfs-image blob** that carries
both the control-plane `.blob`s and the bootable `/rootfs`, and **activate it by
loop-mounting** that image. Register = seal, deregister = remove.

```
        ┌──────────────────────── HOST (Artix / s6) ────────────────────────┐
        │  s6d supervises the appliance as ONE unit (incus up/down)          │
        │                                                                    │
        │  op-grpc-bridge ──UDS──▶ appliance gRPC endpoint                   │
        │        ▲                        │                                  │
        │        │ reflection from        │ CallMethod{plugin_id, method}    │
        │        │ appliance blob         ▼                                  │
        │  ActiveReflectionCatalog   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐  │
        │  (tmpfs /dev/shm)          │  INCUS CONTAINER  (bare-metal-like)│  │
        │        ▲ loads /blobs      │  root = /rootfs subvolume (loop-ro)│  │
        │        │                   │  systemd owns:                     │  │
        │  ┌─────┴───────────────┐   │    • netmaker (server)             │  │
        │  │ appliance btrfs img │   │    • netclient  (OQ-1: wg iface)   │  │
        │  │  /blobs/<id>/*.blob │   │    • emqx  (MQTT, replaces mosq.)  │  │
        │  │  /rootfs (bootable) │   │    • exporters / supporting svcs   │  │
        │  │  /blob-index.json   │   │  all inter-service comms LOCAL     │  │
        │  └─────────────────────┘   └───────────────────────────────────┘  │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

No NIC on the container; the only external surface is the UDS the bridge dials.
The WireGuard interface (if OQ-1(a)) is the identity fabric, not general I/O.

---

## Two design forks, resolved

### OQ-2 — composite schema vs aggregate bundle (RECOMMENDATION)

`btrfs.rs` already seals *many* `.blob`s into one image (one subvolume per
plugin) — so a pure "bundle" (child plugins stay separate, nesting lives only in
`blob-index.json`) is almost free but gives you **N D-Bus objects**, not one
appliance. The requirement (REQ-3.1) is a single addressable object.

**Recommendation: hybrid.**

- **Control-plane identity = composite.** One appliance `PluginSchema`
  (`plugin_id = "netmaker_appliance"`) whose schema references the child
  capability schemas (`netmaker`, `netclient`, `emqx`, …) as nested `$defs`,
  with **child subids carried up** (closes `llm_projection.rs:229`). One
  `plugin_id`, one `schema_hash16`, one D-Bus object, one CallMethod surface.
- **At-rest artifact = one image, many subvolumes.** The image still contains
  per-child `/blobs/<child>/…` (reusing the existing multi-blob sealing) **plus**
  the composite appliance blob **plus** `/rootfs`. The child blobs are the
  descriptor/reflection detail; the appliance blob is the addressable identity.

This keeps `CallMethod` routing single-object while reusing the shipped
multi-blob image machinery. Method names are namespaced by child, e.g.
`netmaker.join_network`, `netclient.status`, `emqx.list_clients`.

> Owner confirms the hybrid (or picks pure composite / pure bundle) before
> Phase 2 begins.

### OQ-1 — WireGuard exception

Design assumes **OQ-1(a)** unless the owner says otherwise: `netclient` brings
up the WG interface inside the container as the zero-trust identity fabric;
management and data still ride UDS/gRPC; the container has no *other* NIC. If
OQ-1(b) is chosen, an added task inserts a mesh-membership shim so the container
has zero kernel network interfaces (larger, deferred).

---

## Component 1 — Nested schema aggregation (`op-plugins` / `op-state-store`)

New: a composite-schema builder that takes the child `PluginSchema`s and emits
one appliance `PluginSchema`.

```rust
// crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/appliance/mod.rs (new)
/// Fold child capability schemas into one appliance schema.
/// Deterministic: sorted children, sorted methods, no timestamps (REQ-3.3).
pub fn compose_appliance_schema(
    appliance_id: &str,
    children: &[(&str, PluginSchema)],   // (namespace, child schema)
) -> PluginSchema {
    // 1. Namespace each child method: "<ns>.<method>".
    // 2. Carry every child subid (src/mut/obs/evt/exp) into the appliance
    //    method manifest — do NOT drop nested $defs subids (REQ-3.2).
    // 3. Preserve mut.* actor_id/capability_id and evt.* event_id/event_hash
    //    (REQ-3.4).
    // 4. Emit nested $defs so structure round-trips via schemars_adapter.
}
```

The aggregation is the single place the appliance schema is computed
(one-schema rule). The appliance `schema_hash` is the `op-blob` sha256 over the
canonical composite JSON — reused, not re-implemented.

**Subid carry-up (the actual fix for `llm_projection.rs:229`):** the projection
walks nested `$defs` and appends child subids to the appliance's subid set,
rather than stopping at the top level. New appliance-level subids
(e.g. `exp.service.netmaker-appliance.render@v1`,
`obs.service.netmaker-appliance.status@v1`) are registered in
`oscal_subid_registry.rs`.

---

## Component 2 — `/rootfs` extension of the btrfs image (`op-blob`)

Extend `seal_blobs_into_btrfs_image` (or add a sibling
`seal_appliance_image`) so the staging tree gains a `rootfs/` directory that
`mkfs.btrfs --rootdir` populates as a subvolume alongside `blobs/`.

```
staging/
  blobs/<child>/<child>.<hash16>.blob        (existing)
  blobs/netmaker_appliance/…blob             (composite identity blob)
  rootfs/                                     (NEW subvolume — bootable FS)
    usr/bin/{netmaker,netclient,emqx,…}
    etc/systemd/system/*.service
    etc/emqx/…  etc/netclient/…
  blob-index.json                             (extended: rootfs + appliance id)
```

```rust
// op-blob/src/btrfs.rs (extended)
pub struct ApplianceImageReport {
    pub base: BtrfsImageReport,      // reuse existing fields
    pub has_rootfs: bool,
    pub appliance_id: String,
    pub rootfs_subvol: String,       // "rootfs"
}
```

- Sealing stays `mkfs.btrfs --rootdir --shrink` (mountless, root-free) with an
  extra `--subvol rootfs`.
- `blob-index.json` gains:
  ```json
  {
    "format": "opdbus-blob-image/2",
    "appliance": { "plugin_id": "netmaker_appliance", "schema_hash": "…" },
    "rootfs": { "subvol": "rootfs" },
    "blobs": [ … ]
  }
  ```
- Determinism note (REQ-4.2): file contents/layout are controlled; `mkfs.btrfs`
  metadata (fs UUID) is not guaranteed reproducible — document and, if needed,
  pass a fixed UUID. Any residual non-determinism is recorded, not hidden.

**Activation** (host, on register / boot):

```
mount -o loop,ro <appliance>.img /mnt/opdbus-appliance
# 1. catalog: load /mnt/opdbus-appliance/blobs/* into ActiveReflectionCatalog
# 2. container: incus config the container root to the /rootfs subvolume
#    (btrfs subvol as Incus rootfs); systemd inside boots the stack
```

Runtime plugin reads still come from tmpfs catalog (REQ-8.3 / NFR-2); `/rootfs`
is never copied into `/dev/shm`.

---

## Component 3 — Appliance plugin surface (`op-plugins`)

Replace the host-oriented `netmaker.rs` internals (REQ-7.2) with a
container-internal driver reached over UDS. The plugin's `apply_state` /
method dispatch talks to the container's internal gRPC endpoint (or the
systemd-managed services via that endpoint), never a host `netclient`.

Authoritative Method → child → transport table:

| Appliance method            | Child      | Effect (inside container)                    | subid category |
|---|---|---|---|
| `netmaker.join_network`     | netmaker   | server-side network join                     | `mut`          |
| `netmaker.leave_network`    | netmaker   | server-side leave                            | `mut`          |
| `netmaker.list_networks`    | netmaker   | read networks                                | `obs`          |
| `netclient.status`          | netclient  | wg/mesh status (OQ-1)                         | `obs`          |
| `netclient.restart`         | netclient  | restart internal systemd unit                | `mut`          |
| `emqx.list_clients`         | emqx       | broker client list                           | `obs`          |
| `emqx.get_stats`            | emqx       | broker metrics                               | `obs`          |
| `appliance.status`          | appliance  | aggregate health of all internal units       | `obs`          |
| `appliance.snapshot`        | appliance  | `btrfs send`-able image snapshot             | `mut`          |

Method names, subids, and `required_capability` come from the composite schema
(single source of truth); the table restates them for review, it does not add
them independently.

---

## Component 4 — gRPC bridge / reflection (`op-grpc-bridge`)

- The bridge advertises appliance services from the **appliance blob's
  descriptor set** loaded into `ActiveReflectionCatalog` (REQ-2.3), not a
  static list. Existing container-internal reflection recognition is the seam
  to extend.
- The current `grpc_client.rs::netmaker_*` direct-proto client
  (`netmaker_service_client::NetmakerServiceClient`, `netmaker_join`, …) is
  reviewed: if it bypasses `CallMethod`, it is retargeted through the plugin
  surface (REQ-2.2). No new `operation.<domain>.v1` package.

---

## File layout after this spec

```
crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/
  appliance/mod.rs                  NEW — compose_appliance_schema + subid carry-up
  appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs   NEW — composite plugin (namespaced methods)
  netmaker.rs                       EDIT — drop host-netclient paths (REQ-7.2)
  oscal_subid_registry.rs           EDIT — appliance subids

crates/op-blob/src/
  btrfs.rs                          EDIT — /rootfs subvolume + blob-index v2
  catalog.rs                        (unchanged; consumes /blobs as today)

crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/
  grpc_client.rs                    EDIT — retarget netmaker_* via CallMethod
  (reflection wiring)               EDIT — advertise from appliance blob

deploy/netmaker/
  appliance/                        NEW — single-container build (rootfs staging,
                                          systemd units, emqx + netclient configs)
  incus-compose.yaml                REMOVE/replace (REQ-7.1)
  mosquitto.conf, host-mosquitto.conf  REMOVE (EMQX replaces)
  rumqttd.toml                      REMOVE stale host-broker narrative (REQ-1.4)
```

---

## Determinism & durability

- Appliance `schema_hash` is deterministic over the composite JSON (sorted, no
  timestamps) — the artifact identity in `<plugin_id>.<hash16>.blob`.
- Image byte-determinism is best-effort per REQ-4.2; the schema-blob layer is
  fully deterministic regardless of the rootfs.
- Durability = `op-blockchain` per-mutation chain + btrfs snapshot /
  `send`/`receive`. No SQL for state; no separate snapshot backups.

## What is explicitly NOT changed

- The tmpfs runtime catalog and `catalog_hash` computation (one-schema rule).
- The sealed `OPBLOB01` byte format and section layout.
- Host s6 supervision model; only the *container internals* use systemd.
- Frontend (lovable).

# Tasks — netmaker-appliance-nested-blob

Each task ends with a green gate. Rust gates: `cargo check -p <crate>` (fast),
`cargo clippy … -D warnings` + `cargo fmt --all -- --check` at phase ends.
Phases are ordered so the two open questions are resolved before the expensive
work; nothing here touches the frontend.

---

## Phase 0 — Confirm the two open questions (no code)

### Task 0.1 — Resolve OQ-2 (composite vs bundle) and OQ-1 (WireGuard)
**Requirements**: REQ-3.5, REQ-2.4
**Steps**:
1. Owner confirms the **hybrid composite** recommendation (one appliance
   `plugin_id`, child schemas nested, image carries per-child blobs + rootfs) —
   or selects pure composite / pure bundle.
2. Owner confirms **OQ-1(a)** (WG interface is the identity-fabric exception) or
   selects **OQ-1(b)** (zero kernel NICs, needs a mesh shim → adds Phase 5).
**Acceptance**: both choices recorded at the top of `design.md`. No code until
this is done — it changes Component 1 and Component 2 shapes.

---

## Phase 1 — Nested schema aggregation (control-plane identity)

### Task 1.1 — `compose_appliance_schema` + subid carry-up
**Requirements**: REQ-3.1, REQ-3.2, REQ-3.3, REQ-3.4
**Context**: closes the `common/llm_projection.rs:229` gap (nested `$defs`
subids are not carried today).
**Steps**:
1. Add `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/appliance/mod.rs` with
   `compose_appliance_schema(appliance_id, children)`.
2. Namespace child methods `<ns>.<method>`; fold child `$defs` (reuse
   `schemars_adapter` inlining) into the appliance schema.
3. Walk nested `$defs` and carry every child subid up; preserve `mut.*`
   `actor_id`/`capability_id` and `evt.*` `event_id`/`event_hash`.
4. Unit test: sorted determinism — same children → identical canonical JSON →
   identical `schema_hash` (via `op-blob` seal).
5. Unit test: a child `mut.*`/`evt.*`/`exp.*` subid appears in the composed
   appliance schema (regression against the 229 gap).
**Gate**: `cargo test -p op-plugins appliance::` green.

### Task 1.2 — Register appliance subids
**Requirements**: REQ-3.4, NFR-4
**Steps**:
1. Add appliance-level subids (e.g. `obs.service.netmaker-appliance.status@v1`,
   `mut.service.netmaker-appliance.snapshot@v1`,
   `exp.service.netmaker-appliance.render@v1`) to
   `oscal_subid_registry.rs`.
2. Run the CI subid-uniqueness check.
**Gate**: subid uniqueness test green; `cargo check -p op-plugins` green.

---

## Phase 2 — `/rootfs` extension of the btrfs image

### Task 2.1 — Extend sealing with a `rootfs` subvolume
**Requirements**: REQ-4.1, REQ-4.2, REQ-4.4, NFR-2
**Steps**:
1. In `op-blob/src/btrfs.rs`, add `seal_appliance_image(blob_paths, rootfs_dir,
   appliance_id, image_path)` (or extend the existing fn) that stages `rootfs/`
   next to `blobs/` and passes `--subvol rootfs` to `mkfs.btrfs`.
2. Extend `blob-index.json` to `opdbus-blob-image/2` with `appliance` +
   `rootfs` entries; keep `blobs` backward-compatible.
3. Return `ApplianceImageReport { base, has_rootfs, appliance_id, rootfs_subvol }`.
4. Keep sealing mountless/root-free; document any fs-UUID non-determinism
   (REQ-4.2), pin the UUID if feasible.
5. Unit test with a tiny fake `rootfs/` (a couple of files): superblock magic
   verified, index v2 parses, `has_rootfs == true`.
**Gate**: `cargo test -p op-blob btrfs::` green (skips cleanly if `mkfs.btrfs`
absent, matching existing `which_mkfs` guard).

### Task 2.2 — Activation helper (loop-mount → catalog + rootfs)
**Requirements**: REQ-4.3, REQ-5.1, NFR-2
**Steps**:
1. Add an activation helper that loop-mounts the image ro, loads `/blobs` into
   `ActiveReflectionCatalog` (tmpfs stays authoritative for runtime), and
   returns the `/rootfs` subvol path for Incus.
2. Ensure `/rootfs` is never copied into `/dev/shm` (NFR-2).
**Gate**: `cargo check -p op-blob` green; helper documented with the mount hint.

---

## Phase 3 — Appliance plugin + bridge wiring

### Task 3.1 — `netmaker_appliance` composite plugin
**Requirements**: REQ-1.1, REQ-2.2, REQ-3.1, REQ-6.1
**Steps**:
1. Add `appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs` composing `netmaker`, `netclient`,
   `emqx` via Task 1.1; register it in `default_registry.rs`.
2. Dispatch namespaced methods through the container-internal gRPC endpoint over
   UDS; no polling/watchers.
**Gate**: `cargo check -p op-plugins` green; appliance appears in `ListPlugins`.

### Task 3.2 — Retarget `netmaker.rs` off host-`netclient`
**Requirements**: REQ-1.3, REQ-7.2
**Steps**:
1. Remove/redefine host-`netclient` fields and code paths
   (`installed`/`daemon_running`-under-s6/host `control_socket`,
   `check_netclient_installed`, host config read/write, host `restart_netclient`).
2. Point capability at the container-internal, systemd-owned service.
**Gate**: `cargo check -p op-plugins` green; no host `Command::new` for
`netclient` remains (grep clean).

### Task 3.3 — Bridge reflection from the appliance blob
**Requirements**: REQ-2.1, REQ-2.3
**Steps**:
1. In `op-grpc-bridge`, advertise appliance services from the appliance blob's
   descriptor set (not a static list); reuse existing container-internal
   reflection recognition.
2. Review `grpc_client.rs::netmaker_*`; if it bypasses `CallMethod`, retarget it
   through the plugin surface (no new proto package).
**Gate**: `cargo check -p op-grpc-bridge` green.

---

## Phase 4 — Single-container deploy + cleanup

### Task 4.1 — Single-container appliance build
**Requirements**: REQ-1.1, REQ-1.2, REQ-1.4
**Steps**:
1. Add `deploy/netmaker/appliance/` producing the `rootfs/` staging:
   `netmaker` + `netclient` + `emqx` binaries, `systemd` units, EMQX + netclient
   configs. Bootstrap scripts only (the blessed exception).
2. Wire the staging into `seal_appliance_image` (Task 2.1).
**Gate**: image builds; `verify_btrfs_image` true; `blob-index.json` v2 valid.

### Task 4.2 — Remove stale multi-container / host-broker artifacts
**Requirements**: REQ-1.4, REQ-7.1
**Steps**:
1. Remove/replace `incus-compose.yaml`, `compose.yaml`, `mosquitto.conf`,
   `host-mosquitto.conf`; delete the stale host-broker `rumqttd.toml` narrative.
2. Grep the repo for "host broker" / host-`netclient` docs and reconcile.
**Gate**: `grep -rn "replaces the no-NIC" deploy/` empty; no doc describes a
host broker or host `netclient`.

---

## Phase 5 — (conditional) OQ-1(b) zero-NIC mesh shim
Only if the owner chose OQ-1(b) in Task 0.1. Adds a brokered mesh-membership
path so the container has zero kernel network interfaces. Deferred by default.

---

## Phase 6 — Final audit
**Requirements**: REQ-2.2, REQ-3.3, REQ-5.3, NFR-1
**Steps**:
1. `grep -rn "operation\..*\.v1" crates/` — no new appliance service package.
2. Confirm appliance `schema_hash` is stable across two builds (determinism).
3. Confirm the blob sealer in `op-blob` is the only writer of catalog blobs
   (SchemaEngine only reports the hash).
4. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and
   `cargo fmt --all -- --check` green.
**Gate**: all above green; both open questions recorded as resolved.

Done. Wrote the spec at `.kiro/specs/netmaker-appliance-nested-blob/` (requirements.md, design.md, tasks.md), matching the house `.kiro/specs` format and grounded in the actual source I read.

**What it captures**
- **The vision as end-state**: one self-contained Incus container (systemd-owned internally, host stays s6, no NIC, UDS/gRPC only) holding netmaker + netclient + EMQX → described as **one nested plugin schema** → sealed as **one self-describing btrfs-image blob** → activated by loop-mounting it (`/blobs` feeds the catalog, `/rootfs` is the container root). Register = seal, deregister = remove.
- **What already exists** (so we don't rebuild): `op-blob/src/btrfs.rs` already seals blobs into a mountable/snapshottable/`send`-able btrfs image; `catalog.rs` per-object shm + single-place `catalog_hash`; `blob.rs` deterministic `OPBLOB01` format.
- **The one real gap**: `llm_projection.rs:229` doesn't carry nested `$defs` subids up. The composite-schema aggregation (Phase 1) closes it.
- **The `/rootfs` extension**: the genuinely new blob work (Phase 2) - adding a bootable rootfs subvolume to the image, kept out of `/dev/shm` (NFR-2).

**Two things I deliberately left for you to decide** rather than invent (both flagged as open questions, Phase 0 gates the code):
- **OQ-1**: does netclient's WireGuard interface count as the allowed identity-fabric exception, or must the container have zero kernel NICs (needs a mesh shim)?
- **OQ-2**: composite schema vs aggregate bundle - I recommend the hybrid (one appliance `plugin_id`, child schemas nested, image carries per-child blobs + rootfs) with rationale in design.md.

Note: files are `0600` (kiro-style). Nothing was built or wired - this is spec only. If you confirm OQ-1/OQ-2, I can start Phase 1 (the schema aggregation + subid carry-up, which is the load-bearing piece).

## Two design forks, resolved

### OQ-2 — composite schema vs aggregate bundle (RECOMMENDATION)

`btrfs.rs` already seals *many* `.blob`s into one image (one subvolume per
plugin) — so a pure "bundle" (child plugins stay separate, nesting lives only in
`blob-index.json`) is almost free but gives you **N D-Bus objects**, not one
appliance. The requirement (REQ-3.1) is a single addressable object.

**Recommendation: hybrid.**

- **Control-plane identity = composite.** One appliance `PluginSchema`
  (`plugin_id = "netmaker_appliance"`) whose schema references the child
  capability schemas (`netmaker`, `netclient`, `emqx`, …) as nested `$defs`,
  with **child subids carried up** (closes `llm_projection.rs:229`). One
  `plugin_id`, one `schema_hash16`, one D-Bus object, one CallMethod surface.
- **At-rest artifact = one image, many subvolumes.** The image still contains
  per-child `/blobs/<child>/…` (reusing the existing multi-blob sealing) **plus**
  the composite appliance blob **plus** `/rootfs`. The child blobs are the
  descriptor/reflection detail; the appliance blob is the addressable identity.

This keeps `CallMethod` routing single-object while reusing the shipped
multi-blob image machinery. Method names are namespaced by child, e.g.
`netmaker.join_network`, `netclient.status`, `emqx.list_clients`.

> Owner confirms the hybrid (or picks pure composite / pure bundle) before
> Phase 2 begins.

## Nesting is native (was OQ-2 — resolved)

There is no composite-vs-bundle fork. The appliance is **one composite plugin**
(`plugin_id = "netmaker_appliance"`) whose *state struct nests the child
capability structs* (`netmaker`, `netclient`, `emqx`, …). schemars emits their
`$defs`; `op-blob/src/adapter.rs` inlines them, `descriptor.rs` builds the
nested proto messages, both are sealed into the blob, and the `schema_renderer`
/ `json_render` plugins render them. Result: one `plugin_id`, one
`schema_hash16`, one D-Bus object, one `CallMethod` surface, no bespoke
aggregation layer. Method names are namespaced by child, e.g.
`netmaker.join_network`, `netclient.status`, `emqx.list_clients`.

Subids use the existing plugin-scoped `op_blob::inject_common_subids` pattern.
The adapter intentionally ingests only top-level subids into the uniqueness map,

## Component 1 — Composite appliance plugin (`op-plugins`)

No new aggregation builder. The appliance is an ordinary plugin whose state
struct nests the child capability structs; schemars + `op-blob`'s existing
`$defs` inlining and descriptor builder do the rest.

```rust
// crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/appliance/netmaker_appliance.rs (new)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema, Default)]
#[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "sch.software.plugin.netmaker-appliance.schema@v1"))]
pub struct NetmakerApplianceState {
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.netmaker@v1"))]
    pub netmaker: NetmakerState,      // child struct → emitted as a $def
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.netclient@v1"))]
    pub netclient: NetclientState,    // child struct → emitted as a $def
    #[schemars(extend("x-oscal-subid" = "obs.service.netmaker-appliance.emqx@v1"))]
    pub emqx: EmqxState,              // child struct → emitted as a $def
}
```

<coding_guidelines>
# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

3tched / OP-DBUS: a native, deterministic control plane for Artix Linux infrastructure (s6 supervision, NOT systemd). ~38-crate Rust workspace under `crates/`, plus a Vite/React/shadcn frontend. All source lives inside `crates/` workspace members — never a generic top-level `src/`. Other top-level dirs: `deploy/` (Artix s6 service defs + install scripts), `schemas/` (JSON schemas loaded at runtime), `docs/`. This file is the authoritative agent guidance; where any doc and the tree disagree, the tree wins.

## Build, lint, test

All cargo commands run from the repo root (the workspace root).

```bash
cargo build --workspace                 # build everything
cargo check -p <crate>                  # fast check a single crate (do this before edits)
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features
cargo test -p <crate> <test_name>       # single test
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
```

Frontend — there are **two** Vite apps; don't confuse them:

1. `crates/` (`vite_react_shadcn_ts`, source in `crates/src/`) — the primary UI dev tree; all npm commands below run here.
2. `crates/op-web/ui/` (`zeroclaw-gui-repo`) — the app **op-web actually embeds** (RustEmbed of `ui/dist/`). Its package.json has no `build` script (and build.rs's error message suggesting `npm run build` is stale); rebuild with `npx vite build` from that directory. Building `crates/` does NOT update what op-web serves.

```bash
cd crates
npm run dev / build / lint / typecheck
npm test                                # vitest run
npx vitest run src/test/<file>          # single test file
```

Build gotchas:

- `[patch.crates-io]` pins zbus to a **local checkout at `/home/jeremy/git/zbus`** — the workspace does not build without it.
- `op-web` **release** builds panic unless `crates/op-web/ui/dist/index.html` exists (RustEmbed); build that UI first (`npx vite build` in `crates/op-web/ui`). Dev builds compile with an empty asset set, so the panic only bites on `--release`.
- The root `op-dbus` package has no binary — real binaries live in member crates (`op-web` → `op-web-server`/`opdbus`, `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-cognitive-mcp`, `op-projection` → `projection_server`, `op-s6-systemctl` → `s6d`, etc.).
- `op-ml` is commented out of the workspace (ort API breakage).
- Rust-first: no new Python; scripts are shell.

## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants

**D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`; reads, writes, and tool calls go through it (`PluginService.CallMethod`, or the `zbusctl` operator CLI — installed at `~/.cargo/bin/zbusctl`, not built from this repo). No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops or D-Bus watchers in plugin/service code — bootstrap scripts are the only exception. New backend capabilities are **plugins registered in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`**, never new gRPC proto service packages.

**PluginSchema is the single source of truth.** D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers all derive from the schema; validate inputs against it. Any derived value (e.g. a catalog hash) is computed in exactly one function, one place. Current layout: each plugin defines a `<name>_schema()` function in its own file under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, aggregated via `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`; a runtime JSON loader also reads `schemas/plugin/*.json` (repo root) via `schema_loader.rs`. NOTE: older docs claim all schemas live in a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` — **that file does not exist**; single-file consolidation is planned work (`FACTORY-PROMPT-plugin-schema-uniformization.md`), not present reality.

**The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog in shared memory: `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob` (`op_blob::catalog::DEFAULT_SHM_DIR`). A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog; register = seal, deregister = remove. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob` — never SchemaEngine (`op-projection`'s `write_schemas_to_shm` only reports the published catalog hash via `op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash()`). Consumers read SHM directly (1:1 zero-copy) — they never re-hash, never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder, `live-schema.json` monolith, and manifest are gone; docs that mention them are stale.

**Reactive, not polled.** The system does not watch, poll, or index. SHM is the authoritative present-state that components read; an arrival (e.g. an xray greeting connection) triggers action. Durability is the per-mutation immutable blockchain (`op-blockchain`) — there are no snapshot backups and **no SQL for state** (graph store is CozoDB).

**Transport & identity (zero-trust).** gRPC (tonic, TLS mandatory) over Unix domain sockets internally; containers get **no NIC or IP** — all container I/O is UDS. Identity = WireGuard pubkey → Argon2(PSK, salt=pubkey) sessionid; a container's name IS its sessionid. The xray router injects identity headers (`X-Ghostbridge-Footprint`/`X-WireGuard-Pubkey`) — that header is the only gate; IP ACLs/ports are theater. SESSION bus = the WG-identity-gated plugin surface; SYSTEM bus = local agents/mirror.

**MCP gateways (settled — do not redesign).** `op-cognitive-mcp` is the universal gateway for ALL external clients (tonic-web gRPC :50052 + server reflection for tool discovery). `compact-mcp` is loopback-only for the chatbot. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.

**Host tooling.** Manage s6 services via the `s6d` CLI (from `op-s6-systemctl`), not raw `s6-svc`. OVS is driven natively over OVSDB JSON-RPC via the rovs plugins (`op-openvswitch-daemon` is deprecated — don't extend it). Containers are Incus; expose sockets via `zbusctl createsocket`, not raw incus proxy devices.

## Crate map (the ones you'll actually touch)

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `op-plugins` | Plugin registry + all state plugins + per-plugin schema functions (the schema source) |
| `op-projection` | SchemaEngine — schema registration/audit; reads the published catalog hash (blob sealing lives in `op-blob`) |
| `op-web` | Axum HTTP server, embeds the UI, `opdbus` CLI |
| `op-grpc-bridge` | tonic gRPC bridge (TLS) between D-Bus surface and external clients |
| `op-cognitive-mcp` | External MCP gateway, CozoDB memory, Qdrant semantic search |
| `op-identity` | WireGuard identity, sessionid derivation, sled/shuttle |
| `op-blockchain` | Per-mutation immutable chain (the durability layer) |
| `op-blob` / `op-state-store` | Sealed blob catalog / schema engine storage |
| `op-network` | Native OVSDB, OpenFlow, rtnetlink (no CLI subprocesses) |
| `op-s6-systemctl` | `s6d` service-management CLI |
| `op-xray-daemon` | xray router daemon (identity injection, subdomain routing) |
| `op-gemma` | Gemma inference plugin (schema-driven UI generation) |

## Identifiers (subid taxonomy — mandatory)

Every D-Bus object, plugin, schema, mutation, event, and tool carries a `uuid` (machine identity, never changes) **and** a `subid`:

```
<category>.<component-type>.<subject>.<verb>[.<facet>][@vN]
```

- Exactly seven categories, no others: `src` (authoritative source/ingress), `prj` (D-Bus projection/mirror publication), `sch` (schema/contract/vocabulary), `mut` (write path), `obs` (read/query/discovery), `evt` (emitted signal/audit event/proof), `exp` (consumer-facing render — MCP tool, UI surface, gRPC view).
- Component-type reuses OSCAL vocabulary (`software`, `service`, `network`, `standard`, `validation`, `policy`, …).
- `mut.*` must carry `actor_id` + `capability_id`; `evt.*` must carry `event_id`/`event_hash`.
- `subid` is an OSCAL `prop` (`ns`/`name`/`value`), never embedded in `remarks`; compliance mappings (`control_refs[]` etc.) live in metadata arrays, never inside the subid string.
- Subids are immutable per subject — material meaning changes get a new subject with `@vN`. All subids are registered in the canonical registry (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`); uniqueness is CI-enforced.

Uses `rustables` for atomic updates. 3. **Configuration Parsing:** Load interface configurations specifying DHCP status, static addresses (optional), and the target `nftables_zone`. 4. **Socket Control:** Accept `reload`, `status`, `ping` commands. 5. **(Optional) Docker IP Tracking:** Maintain an internal map of running container IDs to their discovered IP addresses. ### Example Configuration (`/etc/rust-network-mgr/config.yaml`) [Permalink: Example Configuration (/etc/rust-network-mgr/config.yaml)](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#example-configuration-etcrust-network-mgrconfigyaml) ```` ```yaml interfaces: ```` - name: eth0 # Interface name dhcp: true # Monitor DHCP addresses for this interface nftables\_zone: wan # Maps to nftables set 'wan\_ips' in table 'inet filter' - name: eth1 address: 192.168.1.1/24 # Optional static address info (not currently used for monitoring logic) nftables\_zone: lan # Maps to nftables set 'lan\_ips' in table 'inet filter' # ... other interfaces [Permalink: ... other interfaces](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#-other-interfaces) ```` ### NFTables Setup Example This service *expects* a base `nftables` configuration to exist. It only manages the *elements* within predefined sets. Example base `/etc/nftables.conf` snippet: ```nftables table inet filter { set wan_ips { type ipv4_addr flags dynamic } set lan_ips { type ipv4_addr flags dynamic } chain input { type filter hook input priority 0; policy accept; # Example rule using the set ip saddr @wan_ips counter drop } # ... other chains and rules } ```` ### Directory Structure [Permalink: Directory Structure](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#directory-structure) ``` rust-network-mgr/ ├── Cargo.toml ├── src/ │ ├── main.rs │ ├── network.rs │ ├── nftables.rs │ ├── config.rs │ ├── socket.rs │ ├── docker.rs # Docker monitoring module │ └── types.rs ├── tests/ │ ├── basic_tests.rs │ └── nftables_manager_tests.rs # Requires root/nftables access ├── pkg-files/ │ ├── systemd/ │ │ └── rust-network-mgr.service # Example systemd unit │ └── config/ │ └── default.yaml # Example config └── README.md ``` ### Key Rust Dependencies (Current) [Permalink: Key Rust Dependencies (Current)](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#key-rust-dependencies-current) ``` [dependencies] # Core Async/Runtime tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] } futures = "0.3" # Network Monitoring rtnetlink = "0.16.0" netlink-packet-route = "0.22.0" # NFTables Interaction rustables = "0.8.6" # Docker Interaction (Optional Feature) bollard = "0.15" # Configuration serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] } serde_yaml = "0.9" directories = "5.0" # For finding config dirs # Error Handling & Logging anyhow = "1.0" thiserror = "1.0" log = "0.4" env_logger = "0.10" # Or tracing/tracing-subscriber # Utilities nix = "0.27.1" # For Unix socket permissions ``` _(See `Cargo.toml` for the definitive list)_ ### Build, Test, and Run [Permalink: Build, Test, and Run](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#build-test-and-run) - **Build:**`cargo build --release` (Binary at `target/release/rust-network-mgr`) - **Test:**`cargo test` (Some tests require `sudo` and `nftables`) - Run ignored tests: `sudo cargo test -- --ignored` - **Lint:**`cargo clippy` - **Format:**`cargo fmt` - **Run:** - Ensure `/etc/rust-network-mgr/config.yaml` exists or set `RUST_NETWORK_MGR_CONFIG`. - **(Docker)** Ensure the service user has permissions for `/var/run/docker.sock` if Docker monitoring is desired. - Run directly (requires privileges for Netlink/nftables/Docker): `sudo target/release/rust-network-mgr` - Use the example systemd service: Copy `pkg-files/systemd/rust-network-mgr.service` to `/etc/systemd/system/`, then `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`, `sudo systemctl start rust-network-mgr`. Check status with `sudo systemctl status rust-network-mgr` and logs with `sudo journalctl -u rust-network-mgr -f`. ### Control Socket Usage [Permalink: Control Socket Usage](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#control-socket-usage) ``` # Send commands using socat (install if needed: sudo apt install socat) echo "status" | sudo socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/run/rust-network-mgr.sock echo "reload" | sudo socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/run/rust-network-mgr.sock echo "ping" | sudo socat - UNIX-CONNECT:/run/rust-network-mgr.sock ``` ## Development Priorities & Scope [Permalink: Development Priorities & Scope](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#development-priorities--scope) 1. **Reliability:** Ensure correct behavior under various network conditions. 2. **Correctness:** Accurately update `nftables` sets based on monitored IPs. 3. **Simplicity:** Maintain a focused scope on coordinating Netlink events with `nftables` set updates. Optional features like Docker monitoring should be self-contained and fail gracefully. 4. **Testability:** Design components for unit and integration testing. **Current Scope:** This tool focuses primarily on monitoring interface IPs via Netlink and updating _pre-existing_`nftables` sets based on a simple configuration map (`nftables_zone`). It does _not_ manage `nftables` rules, tables, or chains beyond adding/removing IPs from sets. The optional Docker monitoring currently tracks container IPs internally but does not yet integrate them into `nftables` rules. ## Potential Future Features / Roadmap [Permalink: Potential Future Features / Roadmap](https://github.com/sparesparrow/rust-network-mgr#potential-future-features--roadmap) While the core focus is narrow, future enhancements could include: - More sophisticated `nftables` interaction (e.g., managing rules directly). - IPv6 support in `nftables` sets. - **Docker Integration Enhancements:** - Using discovered container IPs in `nftables` rules/sets (e.g., based on container labels or predefined mappings). - Monitoring Docker network attach/detach events for more granular IP tracking. - More detailed status reporting via the control socket (e.g., listing tracked container IPs). _(These are ideas, not commitments. content.text:
I've now read both our socket layer (`shared_socket.rs`, `unix_socket.rs`, `shared_unix_socket.rs`) and rust-network-mgr's architecture. Here's the honest evaluation.

## What rust-network-mgr actually is
- **Netlink IP monitor → nftables sets.** Its core loop watches interface IP add/remove via `rtnetlink` and atomically updates *predefined* `nftables` sets (`wan_ips`, `lan_ips`, `docker_ips`) via `rustables`. That's it for the "network" part.
- **Docker-oriented.** Optional `bollard` monitor tracks *container IPs* from the Docker daemon socket.
- **Its "socket" is a text control channel.** `/run/rust-network-mgr.sock` accepts line commands `reload`/`status`/`ping` (via `socat`). Not a data plane.
- **Adds a TCP REST API (`axum` on `127.0.0.1:9100`) + its own stdio MCP server** (`ureq` → that REST port).

## What "our socket infrastructure" is
- **One shared host UDS** (`/run/ghostbridge/container.sock`) serving the full **tonic gRPC data plane** to all containers, demuxed by gRPC reflection.
- **Identity from `UdsConnectInfo.peer_cred`** → looked up in the identity sled in `/dev/shm` → injects `x-ghostbridge-footprint`. Containers have **no NIC/IP**; UDS only; "IP ACLs/ports are theater."

## Verdict: not a fit for adoption

The mismatches are structural, not superficial:

| Their model | Our invariant |
|---|---|
| IP-based (netlink IPs → nftables IP sets) | Containers have **no IP/NIC**; that whole layer is deliberately unused for the control plane |
| "Socket" = text `reload/status/ping` control channel | Socket = **multiplexed gRPC data plane over UDS** with peer-cred identity |
| Docker/`bollard` | **Incus** + native OVSDB/rtnetlink, no `Command::new` |
| New TCP port `:9100` REST + its own MCP server | **No new ports; gRPC-over-UDS only**; single MCP gateway (`op-cognitive-mcp`) — new MCP shims are explicitly forbidden |

Critically, it doesn't touch any of the things that make **our** socket layer shaky (per SIGNALS): container.sock reflection/surface drift, Incus forkproxy resets, the netmaker `/run` mount crash-loop. It has no UDS data plane, no gRPC, no reflection, no peer-cred identity, no Incus - so it can't stabilize those.

## The one narrow place it *could* matter
The **host** does have real NICs (xray binds `:443`, OVS at the edge). Its `rtnetlink → nftables-set` pattern is a clean reference for host-edge firewalling. But `op-network` already does native `rtnetlink` + OVSDB/OpenFlow, so pulling in a second daemon would duplicate that and violate the single-producer rule.

Bottom line: keep it as a reading reference for rtnetlink/nftables idioms if you want, but it targets a different layer (host IP firewalling + Docker) than our container gRPC-over-UDS problem, and adopting it would fight three of our hard invariants.
